sections.title: Sound of letter dé
paragraphs: The letter is called (dé) /de/. Its main sound is heard in (date) /dat/, a calendar day. The letter makes two sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch the back of your upper front teeth with the tip of your tongue. Stop the air briefly, then release it. Turn your voice on so your throat vibrates. Put your fingers on your throat to feel the buzz.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In most positions, the letter makes its regular sound, as in (mode) /mɔd/. At the end of many words, it is a silent letter and you do not say it, as in (nord) /nɔʁ/ or (chaud) /ʃo/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not touch the gum ridge behind your teeth as in English day. Place your tongue tip directly on the back of your top teeth instead. Do not release a puff of air.
